# Mermoz: fast, agent-first email for Mac (Gmail)

**The mail must go through.** Mermoz is a light, fast email app for macOS, named after the Aéropostale pilot Jean Mermoz. New mail is sorted before you read it. One key handles a thread. Your whole mailbox lives on your Mac, quiet and instant.

Private beta · free and open source · macOS 26 or later · Gmail · version 0.1.3

- Join the private beta: [mermoz.xyz/#beta](https://mermoz.xyz/#beta) (leave the Gmail address you'll use).
- Already invited? [Download Mermoz for Mac](https://github.com/ClementWalter/mermoz/releases/latest/download/Mermoz.dmg).
- Source: [https://github.com/ClementWalter/mermoz](https://github.com/ClementWalter/mermoz).

## Built for a lighter workflow

An inbox that behaves like a flight plan: everything has a status, a destination, and a key to get it there.

- **Sorted before you read it.** Each new email arrives with a suggested status and project. Read it and the suggestion applies, or press `y`.
- **One key, done.** `e` done, `a` archive, `⌫` delete, `⌘Z` undo. Select several with `⇧` and move them together.
- **Flows, not folders.** Unread, To do, Waiting, Done. A list or a board, grouped and ordered your way. Your Gmail labels are your projects.
- **Read what matters.** Original, exactly as sent. Or Optimized: the same words without signatures, disclaimers and quoted history. Made once, kept.
- **Your whole mailbox, instant.** Every message lives on your Mac. Search, read and sort offline, with `⌘K` for anything else.
- **Agent first.** A first-class command line and MCP server. Your agents search, sort and draft; you approve what leaves.

## Your agents fly Mermoz too

Everything the app does, the command line does: search, read, sort, draft. Every command speaks `--json`, and an MCP server plugs Mermoz into Claude, Codex and any agent you run.

- One command per action, scriptable end to end.
- MCP server built in: `mermoz mcp` (stdio). See the [MCP docs](https://mermoz.xyz/docs/mcp/).
- Agents can draft anything. Nothing is sent until you approve it in Mermoz. There is no `--yes`.
- Agents report friction with `mermoz feedback`, so the tool keeps improving.

```text
$ mermoz list --status todo --json
{ "threads": [{ "number": "M-1287", "subject": "Q4 audit — sign by Friday?" }], "total": 1 }
$ mermoz draft reply M-1287 --file reply.md
dft_42  [draft]
$ mermoz send dft_42
error: approval_required: draft dft_42 is waiting for the user to approve it in Mermoz.   # exit 3
```

## The spirit of Mermoz

In 1930, Jean Mermoz flew the Aéropostale mail across the South Atlantic, from Senegal to Brazil, in a little over twenty hours. The Aéropostale pilots had a motto: « Le courrier doit passer », the mail must go through. Mermoz keeps that spirit: mail that moves, light and fast, without the heavy machinery around it.

# Mermoz developer docs

Mermoz keeps your Gmail mailbox on your Mac and lets your own scripts and AI agents work with it. Everything the app does, the command line does, and an MCP server gives agents the same mailbox as native tools. Search and reading are instant and offline. **Agents never send mail on their own**: a send waits in the Review lane until you approve it in Mermoz.

## How the pieces fit

- **`mermozd`**, the daemon inside Mermoz.app, is the only process that touches the network and the mailbox database.
- **`mermoz`**, the command-line tool, and **`mermoz mcp`**, the MCP server, are clients of the daemon over a local Unix socket. Mermoz.app must be running.
- The CLI ships inside the app at `/Applications/Mermoz.app/Contents/Resources/mermoz`. In Mermoz, open **Settings › Developer › Command line tool › Install in PATH** to link it as `mermoz` (into `/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`).

## Pages

- [Mermoz CLI reference](/docs/cli/): every `mermoz` command, with its `--help` text and exit codes.
- [Mermoz MCP server](/docs/mcp/): add Mermoz to Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Codex; the 29 tools and their parameters.
- [Mermoz JSON-RPC protocol](/docs/protocol/): the `mermozd` socket protocol, for building your own client.

## Quick start for agents

```sh
mermoz list --status todo --json          # threads waiting on the user
mermoz search "from:marc audit" --json    # instant, offline full-text search
mermoz thread M-1287 --json               # read a whole thread
mermoz draft reply M-1287 --file r.txt    # draft a reply (never sends)
mermoz send dft_8f2c                      # exit 3: waits for the user's approval
claude mcp add mermoz -- mermoz mcp       # or plug the MCP server into Claude Code
```

Machine-readable summaries: [llms.txt](/llms.txt), [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt), [server.json](/server.json) (MCP registry format) and [/.well-known/mcp.json](/.well-known/mcp.json).

<!-- https://mermoz.xyz/docs/cli/ · updated 2026-10-13 -->

# Mermoz CLI reference

`mermoz` is the command line of Mermoz: the same mailbox as the app, instant and offline, for people and agents. Every command is non-interactive and takes `--json` for machine-readable output. Mermoz.app must be running (the CLI talks to its daemon); otherwise commands exit with code 5.

**Install:** the CLI ships inside the app at `/Applications/Mermoz.app/Contents/Resources/mermoz`. In Mermoz, **Settings › Developer › Command line tool › Install in PATH** links it as `mermoz`.

**Sending:** `mermoz send` never sends by itself. Unless the user turned on agent sending, the draft moves to the Review lane and the command exits with code 3 (`approval_required`): tell the user, do not retry. There is no `--yes`.

## Exit codes

| code | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | error |
| 2 | usage |
| 3 | approval required: tell the user |
| 4 | not found |
| 5 | Mermoz is not running |

## Overview

```text
Your Mermoz mailbox from the terminal. Instant, offline, agent-friendly.

Usage: mermoz [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  accounts      List connected accounts and their sync state
  add-account   Connect a Gmail account, or with --outlook an Outlook one (opens the browser).
  reconnect     Sign an account in to Google again, keeping its mail (opens the browser). Needed when `mermoz accounts` says "sign in again"
  list          List threads, newest first
  labels        List your Gmail labels ("mailboxes") with thread counts
  contacts      Search the directory built from email signatures (name, email or company)
  contact       Show one person's card and recent threads
  search        Full-text search: every word must match, as a whole word, accents and case aside; from:, to:, subject: restrict to a field. Best matches first
  thread        Show a thread with all messages
  conversation  Split or join conversations (Gmail threads read as one chat)
  files         Files shared in any conversation, newest first, optionally matching a name
  attachments   List a thread's attachments, or save them with --out
  status        Set the status of one or more threads
  priority      Set priority: none, urgent, high, normal, low
  project       Add a thread to a project (a Gmail label, created if missing); "none" clears all
  accept        Accept the AI's suggested status and projects for threads (marks them read), or for a whole column with --column (optionally only one --to/--to-project group)
  reject        Turn down the AI's suggestion for threads: they stay where they are and are not suggested again until new mail arrives
  resort        Stop a whole-mailbox sort and clear the suggestions it left that nobody reviewed. Accepted and turned-down suggestions are kept
  suggestions   The AI's pending suggestions in a status column, grouped by where they go, and how far background sorting of that column has got; with --to/--to-project, the threads of that one group (accept them with `mermoz accept`)
  due           Set a follow-up date (YYYY-MM-DD); "none" clears
  rename        Give a thread's card your own title instead of the email subject; --clear shows the subject again. The email itself is not changed
  read          Mark a thread read or unread
  draft         Create and manage drafts
  drive         Google Drive files of a thread, their text, search, saving attachments. Connecting Drive and sharing files happen in the app only
  send          Ask to send a draft. Unless enabled by the user, it waits for approval in Mermoz (exit 3)
  statuses      Workflow statuses
  projects      Projects
  feedback      Report friction with this CLI so it can improve
  chat          Ask the account's AI about a thread (kept with the thread, like in the app). Without a question, shows the conversation so far. Proposals are listed, never applied
  feed          The Feed: open mail as cards, one thing to do each, in order (now, today, this week, waiting on others, can wait)
  later         Put a thread off until a time said in plain words ("vendredi soir", "friday 7pm", "dans 3 jours", "15 nov"; default tomorrow morning). It leaves its column and comes back Unread then, or when new mail arrives. "none" brings it back now
  do            Ask Mermoz to do something to many threads in plain words ("archive all messages
                past 5 months not in done"). The account's AI turns it into a plan; Mermoz shows
                what it would change and how many threads. Dry run unless --yes. Nothing here can
                send, reply to or forward mail.
                  mermoz do "archive everything from news.example older than a month"
                  mermoz do "archive everything from news.example older than a month" --yes
                  mermoz do "delete the promos from shop.example" --yes --confirm 37
                  mermoz do --plan plan.json            A plan written by hand (see docs/protocol.md)
                  mermoz do --undo bop_8f2c             Put every thread of a run back
  router        Instant sorting: the provider in use, whether it has a key, and today's calls. Keys and the provider are changed in the app (Settings › Developer)
  sync          Trigger an immediate sync
  mcp           Run an MCP server on stdio
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json     Machine-readable JSON output
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Examples:
  mermoz list --status todo                 Threads waiting on you
  mermoz search "from:marc audit" --json    Full-text search, JSON output
  mermoz thread M-1287                      Read a whole thread
  mermoz thread M-1287 --conversation       Read every thread of its conversation
  mermoz list --conversations --status todo One row per conversation
  mermoz conversation split M-1290          Take a thread out of its conversation
  mermoz files invoice                      Files shared anywhere, by name
  mermoz attachments M-1287 --out /tmp/a    Save a thread's attachments
  mermoz status M-1287 waiting              Change a thread's status
  mermoz draft reply M-1287 --file r.txt    Draft a reply (never sends)
  mermoz draft new --to a@x.com --body hi --attach plan.pdf --attach photo.jpg
                                            Draft with files (25 MB in total at most)
  mermoz send dft_8f2c                      Ask to send; the user approves in Mermoz
  mermoz chat M-1287 "should I accept?"     Ask the AI about a thread (proposals only)
  mermoz do "archive mail older than 5 months not in done"
                                            Plan a bulk change and show it (--yes runs it)

Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 error · 2 usage · 3 approval required (tell the user) · 4 not found · 5 Mermoz not running
```

## Commands

### mermoz accounts

List connected accounts and their sync state

```text
List connected accounts and their sync state

Usage: mermoz accounts [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  Machine-readable JSON output
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mermoz add-account

Connect a Gmail account, or with --outlook an Outlook one (opens the browser).

```text
Connect a Gmail account, or with --outlook an Outlook one (opens the browser).

A company Google Workspace that blocks Mermoz can sign in through its own
Google Cloud OAuth client (Desktop app) instead:
  mermoz add-account --client-json ~/Downloads/client_secret_….json
  mermoz add-account --client-id ID --client-secret SECRET
That client is stored with the account and used for its Drive too.

Usage: mermoz add-account [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --client-json <CLIENT_JSON>
          The client_secret_*.json downloaded from Google Cloud

      --json
          Machine-readable JSON output

      --client-id <CLIENT_ID>
          OAuth client ID (with --client-secret)

      --client-secret <CLIENT_SECRET>
          OAuth client secret (with --client-id)

      --outlook
          An Outlook account (outlook.com, Hotmail, Live or Microsoft 365) instead

      --wait
          Wait for the browser sign-in to finish and say how it went

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### mermoz reconnect

Sign an account in to Google again, keeping its mail (opens the browser). Needed when `mermoz accounts` says "sign in again"

```text
Sign an account in to Google again, keeping its mail (opens the browser). Needed when `mermoz accounts` says "sign in again"

Usage: mermoz reconnect [OPTIONS] <ACCOUNT>

Arguments:
  <ACCOUNT>  Account id or email

Options:
      --json  Machine-readable JSON output
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mermoz list

List threads, newest first

```text
List threads, newest first

Usage: mermoz list [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json               Machine-readable JSON output
      --status <STATUS>    Status key(s), comma separated (unread, todo, waiting, archive, ...)
      --project <PROJECT>  Project, i.e. Gmail label name (e.g. "Clients/Acme")
      --account <ACCOUNT>  Account email or id
      --label <LABEL>      Gmail label ("mailbox") name, e.g. "Clients/Acme"
      --conversations      One row per conversation (the thread leading it), as in the app
      --feeds              Only automated senders and mailing lists (implies --conversations)
      --limit <LIMIT>      [default: 50]
  -h, --help               Print help
```

### mermoz search

Full-text search: every word must match, as a whole word, accents and case aside; from:, to:, subject: restrict to a field. Best matches first

```text
Full-text search: every word must match, as a whole word, accents and case aside; from:, to:, subject: restrict to a field. Best matches first

Usage: mermoz search [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...

Arguments:
  [QUERY]...  

Options:
      --json           Machine-readable JSON output
      --limit <LIMIT>  [default: 20]
      --gmail          Search all of Gmail instead (Gmail's own syntax), for mail Mermoz doesn't hold
  -h, --help           Print help
```

```text
  -h, --help    Print help
```

### mermoz accept

Accept the AI's suggested status and projects for threads (marks them read), or for a whole column with --column (optionally only one --to/--to-project group)

```text
Accept the AI's suggested status and projects for threads (marks them read), or for a whole column with --column (optionally only one --to/--to-project group)

Usage: mermoz accept [OPTIONS] [THREADS]...

Arguments:
  [THREADS]...  

Options:
      --column <COLUMN>           Every pending suggestion of this status column
      --json                      Machine-readable JSON output
      --to <TO>                   Only the group going to this status ("none": groups that only add projects)
      --to-project <TO_PROJECTS>  Only the group adding exactly these projects (repeat for several)
  -h, --help                      Print help

Examples:
  mermoz accept M-12 M-14
  mermoz accept --column backlog
  mermoz accept --column backlog --to archive --to-project Receipts
```

### mermoz reject

Turn down the AI's suggestion for threads: they stay where they are and are not suggested again until new mail arrives

```text
Turn down the AI's suggestion for threads: they stay where they are and are not suggested again until new mail arrives

Usage: mermoz reject [OPTIONS] <THREADS>...

Arguments:
  <THREADS>...  

Options:
      --json  Machine-readable JSON output
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mermoz resort

Stop a whole-mailbox sort and clear the suggestions it left that nobody reviewed. Accepted and turned-down suggestions are kept

```text
Stop a whole-mailbox sort and clear the suggestions it left that nobody reviewed. Accepted and turned-down suggestions are kept

Usage: mermoz resort [OPTIONS] --stop

Options:
      --json  Machine-readable JSON output
      --stop  
  -h, --help  Print help

Examples:
  mermoz resort --stop
```

### mermoz suggestions

The AI's pending suggestions in a status column, grouped by where they go, and how far background sorting of that column has got; with --to/--to-project, the threads of that one group (accept them with `mermoz accept`)

```text
The AI's pending suggestions in a status column, grouped by where they go, and how far background sorting of that column has got; with --to/--to-project, the threads of that one group (accept them with `mermoz accept`)

Usage: mermoz suggestions [OPTIONS] [STATUS]

Arguments:
  [STATUS]  

Options:
      --ask                       First ask the AI about the column's newest --limit threads (at most 50), as ✨ on the column does
      --json                      Machine-readable JSON output
      --clear                     Clear every suggestion on read threads that nobody reviewed (Unread mail keeps its own); accepted and turned-down ones are kept
      --to <TO>                   List the threads going to this status ("none": groups that only add projects)
      --to-project <TO_PROJECTS>  List the threads going to exactly these projects (repeat for several)
      --limit <LIMIT>             Most threads to list [default: 50]
  -h, --help                      Print help

Examples:
  mermoz suggestions backlog --ask
  mermoz suggestions backlog
  mermoz suggestions backlog --to archive
  mermoz suggestions backlog --to none --to-project Receipts
```

### mermoz due

Set a follow-up date (YYYY-MM-DD); "none" clears

```text
Set a follow-up date (YYYY-MM-DD); "none" clears

Usage: mermoz due [OPTIONS] <THREAD> <DATE>

Arguments:
  <THREAD>  
  <DATE>    

Options:
      --json  Machine-readable JSON output
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mermoz draft

Create and manage drafts

```text
Create and manage drafts

Usage: mermoz draft [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  reply   Draft a reply; recipients and subject default from the thread
  new     Draft a new message
  attach  Add files to a draft
  detach  Remove an attachment from a draft (ids are shown by `draft show`)
  list    List drafts (optionally by state: draft, review, rejected)
  show    Show a draft
  edit    Replace a draft's body
  delete  Delete a draft
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json  Machine-readable JSON output
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mermoz drive

Google Drive files of a thread, their text, search, saving attachments. Connecting Drive and sharing files happen in the app only

```text
Google Drive files of a thread, their text, search, saving attachments. Connecting Drive and sharing files happen in the app only

Usage: mermoz drive [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  files   Drive files linked in a thread, shared with its people, and attachments saved
  read    A Drive file's text (Docs as Markdown, Sheets as CSV, Slides as text)
  search  Search Drive by name and content; no words lists recently opened files
  save    Save an attachment to Drive, in Mermoz/<thread's project>
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json  Machine-readable JSON output
  -h, --help  Print help
```

Put a thread off until a time said in plain words ("vendredi soir", "friday 7pm", "dans 3 jours", "15 nov"; default tomorrow morning). It leaves its column and comes back Unread then, or when new mail arrives. "none" brings it back now

### mermoz do

Ask Mermoz to do something to many threads in plain words ("archive all messages

```text
Ask Mermoz to do something to many threads in plain words ("archive all messages
past 5 months not in done"). The account's AI turns it into a plan; Mermoz shows
what it would change and how many threads. Dry run unless --yes. Nothing here can
send, reply to or forward mail.
  mermoz do "archive everything from news.example older than a month"
  mermoz do "archive everything from news.example older than a month" --yes
  mermoz do "delete the promos from shop.example" --yes --confirm 37
  mermoz do --plan plan.json            A plan written by hand (see docs/protocol.md)
  mermoz do --undo bop_8f2c             Put every thread of a run back

Usage: mermoz do [OPTIONS] [SENTENCE]...

Arguments:
  [SENTENCE]...  What to do, in plain words

Options:
      --json               Machine-readable JSON output
      --yes                Run the plan (otherwise only show it)
      --confirm <CONFIRM>  Deleting needs the number of threads, as the preview shows it
      --plan <PLAN>        A plan as JSON (a file, or - for stdin) instead of asking the AI
      --undo <UNDO>        Undo a run by its id
      --history            The last runs, newest first
  -h, --help               Print help
```

<!-- https://mermoz.xyz/docs/mcp/ · updated 2026-10-13 -->

# Mermoz MCP server

`mermoz mcp` runs an MCP server on **stdio** that gives AI agents the user's Mermoz mailbox as 29 tools: search, read, sort, draft, Drive files and more. It is local: it runs on the user's Mac, next to Mermoz.app, and talks to the app's daemon over a Unix socket. There is no hosted or remote (Streamable HTTP) endpoint: Mermoz has no server of its own that holds mail.

- **Requires:** Mermoz.app installed and running (macOS 26 or later), signed in to Gmail. If the app isn't running, tools answer "Mermoz isn't running. Ask the user to open Mermoz.app."
- **Command:** `mermoz mcp` once the CLI is in PATH (Mermoz › Settings › Developer › Install in PATH), or the full path `/Applications/Mermoz.app/Contents/Resources/mermoz mcp`.
- **Protocol version:** 2025-06-18; capability `tools`.
- **Sending:** `send_draft` moves the draft to the user's Review lane and returns `approval_required` unless the user enabled agent sending. Tell the user; do not retry.

## Add Mermoz to Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add mermoz -- mermoz mcp
# for every project: claude mcp add --scope user mermoz -- mermoz mcp
```

## Add Mermoz to Claude Desktop

Claude Desktop does not read your shell's PATH, so use the full path. In Claude Desktop, **Settings › Developer › Edit Config** opens `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`; add:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mermoz": {
      "command": "/Applications/Mermoz.app/Contents/Resources/mermoz",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Then quit and reopen Claude Desktop.

## Add Mermoz to Codex

```sh
codex mcp add mermoz -- mermoz mcp
```

Or in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.mermoz]
command = "mermoz"
args = ["mcp"]
```

## Any other MCP client

Launch `mermoz mcp` (or `/Applications/Mermoz.app/Contents/Resources/mermoz mcp`) as a stdio server: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdin and stdout. Discovery documents: [server.json](/server.json) (official MCP registry format) and [/.well-known/mcp.json](/.well-known/mcp.json).

## Tools

### search_mail

Full-text search across all local mail (instant, offline). Supports from:, to:, subject: prefixes. Returns threads best match first.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default 20) |
| `query` | string | yes | search words |

### list_threads

List threads (issues) filtered by status/project/account, newest first. Statuses: unread, todo, waiting, in_progress, backlog, review, done, archive, deleted. Projects are the user's Gmail labels; each thread lists its `projects` and the AI's pending `suggestion`. `suggested`: true for threads with a pending suggestion, or {status, projects} for one destination listed by column_suggestions. `conversations`: one row per conversation (Gmail threads with the same people about the same matter, as the user sees them), each with `conversation_threads`; `kind`: ["feed", "list"] for automated senders and mailing lists.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account_id` | string | no | account id |
| `conversations` | boolean | no |  |
| `kind` | array of string | no |  |
| `label_id` | string | no | Gmail label id from list_labels (pass its account_id too) |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default 50) |
| `project` | string | no | project (Gmail label) name |
| `status` | array of string | no |  |
| `suggested` | boolean or object | no |  |

### get_thread

Read a whole thread: every message's plain-text body, recipients and attachment ids. With `conversation`, every message of the conversation it belongs to (each with its `thread_id`), plus its people, files and links.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conversation` | boolean | no |  |
| `id` | string | yes | thread id or number like M-1287 |

### split_conversation

Take a thread out of the conversation Mermoz grouped it into (when it is a different matter). Final: it is never grouped with them again.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | thread id or number |

### merge_conversations

Join the conversations of two or more threads into one (same people, same matter).

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` | array of string | yes |  |

### list_files

Files shared in any conversation, newest first, with their attachment id (read with get_attachment) and thread.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default 50) |
| `query` | string | no | part of a file name |

### update_thread

Change a thread's status, priority (0 none,1 urgent,2 high,3 normal,4 low), projects (Gmail labels: add_projects/remove_projects, or projects to replace) or due date (YYYY-MM-DD, null clears). 'deleted' moves the thread to Gmail Trash.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `add_projects` | array of string | no |  |
| `due` | string or null | no |  |
| `id` | string | yes | thread id or number |
| `priority` | integer | no |  |
| `projects` | array of string | no |  |
| `remove_projects` | array of string | no |  |
| `status` | string | no | status key |

### accept_suggestions

Accept the AI's pending suggestion (status, projects, priority) for threads; they count as read. Pass `ids`, or `column` (a status) to accept that column's pending suggestions — all of them, or only the group given by `to_status`/`to_projects` as listed by column_suggestions.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `column` | string | no | status key of the column |
| `ids` | array of string | no |  |
| `to_projects` | array of string | no |  |
| `to_status` | string or null | no | group's target status (null: groups that only add projects) |

### reject_suggestions

Turn down the AI's pending suggestion for threads: they stay where they are and are not suggested again.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` | array of string | yes |  |

### column_suggestions

The AI's pending suggestions in status columns, grouped by target (status + projects) with counts, and how far background sorting has got (classified of total). Nothing moves until accepted.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account_id` | string | no | limit to an account |
| `project` | string | no | limit to a project |
| `statuses` | array of string | yes |  |

### stop_resort

Stop a whole-mailbox sort and clear every suggestion on read threads that nobody reviewed. Accepted and turned-down suggestions are kept; Unread mail keeps its own.

No parameters.

### get_attachment

Get an attachment's local file path (readable offline); text attachments also return their content.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | attachment id from get_thread |

### create_draft

Create a draft. With thread_id it is a reply and recipients/subject default from the thread. Drafts never send by themselves. Attachments are copied into Mermoz; Gmail sends at most 25 MB of files per email.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attachments` | array of string | no | files to attach: absolute paths |
| `body` | string | yes | plain text body |
| `cc` | array of string | no |  |
| `forward_attachments` | array of string | no | attachment ids from get_thread to send again (forwarding) |
| `subject` | string | no | subject |
| `thread_id` | string | no | thread to reply to |
| `to` | array of string | no |  |

### send_draft

Ask to send a draft. Unless the user enabled agent sending, the draft goes to the user's Review lane and this returns approval_required: tell the user, do not retry.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | draft id |

### search_contacts

Search the user's directory, built automatically from email signatures: names, titles, companies, phones, addresses, websites. Empty query lists recent contacts.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default 20) |
| `query` | string | no | name, email or company |

### list_labels

The user's Gmail labels (mailboxes) with ids, accounts and thread counts.

No parameters.

### list_statuses

Workflow statuses.

No parameters.

### list_projects

Projects: the user's Gmail labels. A thread can be in several.

No parameters.

### chat_about_thread

Ask the user's own AI (the one allowed for the thread's account in Mermoz) about a thread; it sees the thread, its people, status and the user's earlier mail with them, and may search the web. The conversation is kept with the thread and shown in the app. Returns the answer and proposed actions (status, project, follow_up date, draft_reply body); nothing is applied: use update_thread or create_draft to act. Without a question, returns the conversation so far.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | thread id or number |
| `question` | string | no | what to ask |
| `research` | boolean | no | allow web search (default True) |

### thread_drive_files

Google Drive files of a thread: those linked in its messages (with access: ok, no_access or not_connected), files shared by or with its participants, and its attachments already saved to Drive. Needs the account's Drive connected in Mermoz.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | thread id or number |

### read_drive_file

A Google Drive file's text: Docs as Markdown, Sheets as CSV (first sheet), Slides as text, plain-text files as they are. Cached locally.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account_id` | string | yes | account id |
| `file_id` | string | yes | Drive file id |

### search_drive

Search the account's Google Drive by name and content; without a query, the files the user opened most recently.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account_id` | string | yes | account id |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default 20) |
| `query` | string | no | words to find |

### save_attachment_to_drive

Save an attachment to the user's Google Drive, in Mermoz/&lt;the thread's project&gt; (created if missing). Returns the folder and an Open in Drive link; saving again returns the same file. Sharing files stays with the user in the app.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | attachment id from get_thread |

### feed

The user's Feed: every open thread as a card (one thing to do), in sections now, today, week, waiting, later, ordered by deadline then urgency. Each card has a kind (reply, decision, sign, promise, event, payment, intro, waiting, cleanup, reading, other), plain-language reasons, the deadline and amount written in the mail, and the AI's words when written. Automated mail and newsletters come as batch cards listing their threads.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | string | no | only this project's cards |

### snooze_thread

Later: hide threads from the Feed until a time (Unix ms) or until new mail arrives in them. until null brings them back now.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` | array of string | yes |  |
| `until` | integer or null | no |  |

### plan_bulk_action

Plan a change to many threads from a plain-words instruction ("archive all messages past 5 months not in done"), the way the user's Ask Mermoz bar does: the user's own AI turns it into a typed plan (filters + set status / add or remove project / mark read or unread / later / delete to Trash; nothing can send, reply or forward), and Mermoz previews it: a sentence per step, how it was understood, counts per status and sample subjects. Nothing changes. Pass `plan` (the same JSON shape as a returned `plan`) instead of `sentence` to skip the AI. Show the user the summary, then call run_bulk_action.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pick` | object | no | a `pick` from the returned `choices` ({from} or {subject_prefix}): plan with exactly that filter |
| `plan` | object | no | a plan as returned in `plan` |
| `rounds` | array of object | no | when it answered with a question: [{question, answer}] so far (at most 2) |
| `sentence` | string | no | what to do, in plain words |

### run_bulk_action

Run a plan from plan_bulk_action. `confirm` must be the plan's `total` (the number of threads it changes), as a confirmation that the preview was read. Applies in batches and returns the run id for undo_bulk_action.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | integer | yes | the plan's total |
| `id` | string | yes | plan id from plan_bulk_action |

### undo_bulk_action

Put every thread a bulk run changed back as it was.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | run id |

### submit_feedback

Report friction with these tools (missing option, confusing result, slowness) so Mermoz can improve.

| parameter | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes | what went wrong or is missing |
| `tool` | string | no | tool name |
